LMP3.title: United Autosports open LMP3 account with a one-two at Silverstone
LMP3.dek: Brundle, Guasch and England won the 19-car LMP3 class in United's #2 Ligier, a lap clear of the sister car, after starting 18th and leading from the first lap.

chapters.title: A big LMP3 field arrives
text: The 4 Hours of Silverstone opened the 2016 European Le Mans Series and brought the biggest LMP3 turnout the series had seen: 19 cars started, almost all of them Ligier JS P3s powered by Nissan. The one exception was the Ginetta run by Murphy Prototypes, a rented stand-in while its own Ave-Riley car was readied for Imola.

United Autosports arrived with two Ligiers. The #2 paired Alex Brundle and Michael Guasch with Christian England, a returning racer who had been away from the sport for more than a decade, while the #3 carried Mark Patterson, Matthew Bell and Wayne Boyd. Graff and Duqueine each fielded two cars.
Practice was wet and said little about the dry pace. Dino Lunardi's Duqueine topped both Friday sessions, with Graff's cars close behind in the afternoon.

chapters.title: Kaiser snatches pole by 0.051s
text: Qualifying was held in the wet and the LMP3 session was crowded. Lunardi set an early 2:13.315 that looked safe for pole in the #19 Duqueine, but Ross Kaiser found a lap of 2:13.264 at the last moment to put the #6 360 Racing Ligier on top by 0.051s.

Enzo Guibbert's #9 Graff Ligier was third, ahead of Brundle's #2 and Bell's #3 for United, who ended up fourth and fifth on the class grid On the combined grid the pole sitter began from 14th and United's lead car from 18th. Gachet, Nicolet and Rayhall were among those who ran off in the conditions, and just three LMP3 cars failed to out-qualify the GTE field.

chapters.title: Carnage at the start, Brundle leads
text: The opening lap was chaotic, with cars spinning in the first corners and several drivers saying nobody had weaved to warm tyres on the way round. Brundle picked his way through the melee and took the lead from the pole car before the end of the first lap, while the #15 RLR and #19 Duqueine both spun and had to rejoin at the back.

Within a quarter of an hour Brundle led by more than six seconds, and Bell soon got the #3 past Laurent's M.Racing Ligier for a United one-two. Villorba Corse's #7 and By Speed Factory's #5 both stopped on track before the hour was out.

chapters.title: United swap the lead, Graff move up
text: The first round of stops put the #3, now with Patterson at the wheel, ahead of the sister car, while the #2 handed to Guasch. M.Racing's #18 had been running on the podium before a problem dropped it down the order, and it did not reach the flag; the Murphy Ginetta also stopped for good.
Trouillet in the #9 Graff passed Patterson for second, and Smiechowski's Inter Europol Ligier briefly took third. By the end of the hour Guasch held a lead of about 22 seconds in the #2.

chapters.title: Strategy decides the order
text: The second round of stops began with the #20 Duqueine being pushed back into the garage. Patterson, as a bronze-rated driver, had to complete two hours, so the #3 stayed with him and rejoined in the lead; a third stop for fuel and tyres with about 1h40 to go dropped it to sixth and handed the lead back to the #2.

England and Graff's Petit then ran within half a second of each other, with Petit leading for the first time before England took the place back. With an hour left the top five were the #2, #9, #13, #3 and #6.

chapters.title: England holds on, Boyd closes
text: England stayed in the #2 for the final stint. When Graff's #9 made its last scheduled stop, a brief rain shower fell but did not change the race, and England rejoined with a lead of about 23 seconds. Under the late full-course yellow the #2 stopped for a minimal splash of fuel, which made the finish much safer.

Further back, the #3 had lost time when Patterson handed to Boyd and fell to sixth in class, but Boyd lapped much faster than the cars ahead and passed Guibbert's #9 into Maggots with about 30 minutes left. The yellow cost him any chance of catching England, and United finished one-two, with the #3 a lap behind.

chapters.title: United's one-two, Graff on the podium
text: Brundle, Guasch and England won in the #2, completing 113 laps, with Patterson, Bell and Boyd second in the #3, a lap down. Graff's #9 of Trouillet, Petit and Guibbert was third, level on laps with the #3 at 112, and the #19 Duqueine of Hallyday and Lunardi was fourth on the same tally. The pole-sitting 360 Racing #6 completed 111 laps for fifth; Brundle set the class fastest lap, a 1:55.817.

Race Performance's #8 was sixth and Panis Barthez's #16 seventh among the 13 classified runners. Six cars were not classified, among them the Eurointernational #11, Inter Europol #13, Murphy #14, M.Racing #18, By Speed Factory #5 and Villorba Corse #7.
Brundle called it a day when everything fell right and singled out the early lead and the fuel call under yellow. The second round of the championship is at Imola in May.

facts.v: United Autosports finished first and second in its first ELMS race, with England completing the win for the #2 Ligier.
Kaiser's 2:13.264 in the wet put the 360 Racing Ligier ahead of Lunardi's Duqueine.

one.label: Sportscar365: Beche Puts TDS on Pole for 4H Silverstone

facts.v: United brought the #2 in under the late full-course yellow for the minimum fuel needed to reach the flag.
The 360 Racing Ligier was given a stop-go penalty for overtaking under double yellows with about 90 minutes to go.

LMGTE.title: Beechdean Aston inherits Silverstone GTE win after JMW exclusion
LMGTE.dek: Howard, Turner and MacDowall's Beechdean Aston Martin was promoted to the win when JMW's Ferrari was excluded, with AT Racing second and Stanaway's pole-sitting Aston third after a penalty.

chapters.title: Nine GTE cars, three makes
text: The 2016 GTE field was small but varied, with nine cars at Silverstone from Ferrari, Porsche and Aston Martin. Eight were full-season entries, joined by a late one-off: Roald Goethe's #96 Aston Martin, run with Stuart Hall and factory driver Richie Stanaway.

Beechdean's #99 Aston had a changed line-up, with Darren Turner in for Jonny Adam, who stayed with his British GT commitments, alongside Andrew Howard and Alex MacDowall. Formula Racing arrived as defending champions in the #60 Ferrari, with Christina Nielsen added to the crew. Proton fielded two Porsche 911 RSRs, the #77 featuring ELMS newcomer Michael Hedlund. JMW's #66 Ferrari, with Bertolini, was first reserve for Le Mans.

The weekend was dominated by the weather. Teams had only three sets of full-wet Dunlops for the weekend, so many ran few laps in the wet Friday morning, and AT Racing's Ferrari was fastest in the drier second session.

chapters.title: Stanaway on pole in the wet
text: Stanaway went out first in the short wet qualifying session, waiting for a clear track, and improved steadily from a 2:20.9 to a 2:19.348 to take pole for Aston Martin Racing's #96.

Nobody else broke into the 2:19s. Lietz closed to within 0.938s late on to put the #88 Proton Porsche second, and Bertolini's JMW Ferrari was third. Matt Griffin's AF Corse Ferrari and Pier Guidi's AT Racing car followed. Beechdean's #99 qualified seventh in the class.

chapters.title: Hall leads, the Ferraris get tangled
text: Hall led away in the pole Aston, with a few prototypes getting between him and MacDowall, whose #99 had climbed to second after starting seventh in class. AT Racing made an early stop, bringing in Talkanitsa Jr for Pier Guidi.

Duncan Cameron's #55 AF Corse Ferrari had a rough hour, spun by a Duqueine LMP3 and later touched by its sister car. The first full-course yellow, for the prototypes at Luffield, found the two Astons running one-two.

chapters.title: Strategies split
text: AT Racing briefly led after a fast stop without a tyre change, then dropped to fourth when it took tyres. MacDowall's #99 moved up to second, with the #96 close behind. JMW's Ferrari was fourth, and the team clearly planned to run each driver in one long stint.

chapters.title: Turner pulls clear
text: MacDowall and Hall ran about two seconds apart, with the JMW Ferrari 30 seconds behind. After the Astons changed drivers, Turner took the #99 into the lead and was 12 seconds clear by lap 81.
Behind, Lietz lost fourth in class to Talkanitsa Jr, Aaron Scott got the #55 back to fifth, and Seefried picked up a puncture in the #77 after contact with an LMP2 car.

chapters.title: Contact at Vale, then a disqualification
text: With just over 50 minutes left, Turner pitted the #99 from the lead and Howard took it to the flag, which put the JMW Ferrari in front. Howard ran second, with Pier Guidi third in the AT Ferrari, lapping faster but more than a minute behind, and Stanaway in the #96 fourth.

In the closing minutes Stanaway caught Pier Guidi and the two made heavy contact at Vale. The Aston limped over the line ahead with a damaged wheel, but the stewards gave it a four-minute penalty for avoidable contact, and as the Ferrari crossed the line more than three minutes later their places were reversed. A full-course yellow for a loose LMP2 wheel with 19 minutes left had let JMW make its last fuel stop under less pressure.

chapters.title: Beechdean inherit the win
text: JMW took the chequered flag but was excluded after the race, so the win passed to the Beechdean-backed Aston of Howard, Turner and MacDowall, who completed 109 laps. AT Racing's Ferrari of the Talkanitsas and Pier Guidi, level on laps, was promoted to second, with Stanaway, Hall and Goethe in the #96 Aston third after their time penalty.

The AF Corse #55 of Cameron, Griffin and Scott was fourth, a lap down. Formula Racing's #60 was fifth, Proton's #88 sixth and AF Corse's #51 of Perazzini, Cioci and Aguas seventh, all on 108 laps, with Proton's #77 eighth. Lietz set the class fastest lap, a 2:01.241. The next round is at Imola in May.

facts.v: The #66 Ferrari failed post-race scrutineering for an incorrect front splitter and lost what would have been the team's first win in over three years.

one.label: Sportscar365: JMW Ferrari Excluded from 4H Silverstone; AMR Inherits Win

facts.v: Stanaway was penalised four minutes for avoidable contact with the AT Racing Ferrari, demoting the #96 Aston behind it.
Dunlop supplied three sets of full-wet and five of intermediate tyres to each GTE team for the weekend, which limited their running in practice.
Stanaway's 2:19.348 put the Aston almost a second clear of Lietz's Porsche.
